scope: Original schedule and callback bodies on declared synthetic inputs, not historical loader replay.
checks: Piecewise offsets equal independently summed prior batches
New batch applies at boundary, old batch owns preceding step
Boundary starts at offset twelve
Offset twenty is not current batch times step
Batch intervals are consecutive and their inverse returns owner
Step-four mixture offset twenty fails eight-sequence alignment
Configured fractions differ from whole-block allocation
Changing past batch schedule moves next logical sequence by minus twelve
Nominal positions are explicitly fixed-length arithmetic
Equal endpoint offsets do not prove identical consumed batch prefix
Future-only declaration change preserves consumed prefix
Original conversion uses cumulative offset
Original conversion preserves final negative sentinel
Original constructor rejects unaligned converted stage
Conversion negative sentinel is not supported by constructor alignment guard
Stage callback emits only on stage changes
Removed component key is omitted rather than explicitly logged zero
Logged configured weights are not measured batch counts
Reviewer rejects negative_batch
Reviewer rejects missing_zero
Reviewer rejects duplicate_start
Reviewer rejects invalid_block
Reviewer rejects nan_weight
Positive tiny component can round to zero with an explicit warning
Aligned step boundary passes declaration review
Actual CLI writes hashed input and no actual token claims
Actual CLI refuses output overwrite and preserves bytes

synthetic_review.scope:
Review declared schedules, not actual consumed tokens. Uses archived pure-Python
BatchSchedule and mixture allocation helper; no JAX, loader, token replay or training.
Usage: python scripts/audit_batch_clock.py input.json output.json
